authority.source: openssl-3.6.4 crypto/bn/bn_gf2m.c (BN_GF2m_add, BN_GF2m_mod_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_mul_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_sqr_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_exp_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_inv and the wrappers), crypto/bn/bn_mont.c (BN_MONT_CTX_set/copy/set_locked, BN_to/from_montgomery, BN_mod_mul_montgomery, BN_mod_exp_mont, BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime, BN_mod_exp_mont_word, BN_mod_exp2_mont) and crypto/bn/bn_recp.c (BN_RECP_CTX_set, BN_div_recp, BN_reciprocal, BN_mod_mul_reciprocal, BN_mod_exp_recp).
authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, allocator-seam coordinate or unsafe lint attribute changed. Doc comments on the # Safety sections now state the aliasing contract explicitly; no signature or behaviour change for distinct-output calls.
external_contracts: The OpenSSL BIGNUM entry points accept a result object that aliases an input operand. The implementation must compute from the original operands and then write the result; reading an operand after a partial write is a compatibility defect, and forming two live Rust borrows of one allocation is UB.
The two BN_div outputs may be the same object. BN_div stores the remainder first and the quotient last, so that object ends holding the quotient; BN_div_recp inherits this through its delegation.

BN_MONT_CTX and BN_RECP_CTX are opaque context types distinct from BIGNUM. Passing one allocation as both a context and a BIGNUM is not a supported input. BN_MONT_CTX_copy(to == from) returns before forming any borrow.

boundaries.mechanism: BIGNUM-output borrow ordering in BN_GF2m_add, BN_GF2m_mod_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_mul_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_sqr_arr and BN_GF2m_mod_exp_arr
boundaries.contract: r may alias a or b (and both simultaneously). Inputs are cloned before r is borrowed; nothing reads an operand after r is written. The modulus is an int-array/separate BIGNUM snapshot and is never aliased with r.
residuals: The modulus argument (p / the exponent array) is a distinct object/array in the supported contract. A caller passing the same storage as both a modulus and an output is outside the contract; the modulus is nevertheless snapshotted before the write, so the GF2m wrappers remain borrow-safe in that case.
BN_GF2m_poly2arr writes an int array while reading a BIGNUM; the int[]/BIGNUM cross-type alias is not a supported input.

boundaries.mechanism: blinded inversion and division wrappers (mod_inv_vartime, BN_GF2m_mod_inv, BN_GF2m_mod_div and the _arr wrappers)
boundaries.contract: r may alias a/xx/y; each operand is copied before r is first written. The blinded sequence reads a and the modulus before the first BN_GF2m_mod_mul writes r.
residuals: If a caller aliases r with the BIGNUM modulus, the first write changes the modulus used by the later blinded steps. That matches the authority's evaluation order (garbage-in/garbage-out, no UB) but is not a supported result case and is not claimed as one.

boundaries.contract: MontCtx and BigNum are distinct object types; no supported alias exists. BN_MONT_CTX_set reads the modulus before borrowing the context. BN_MONT_CTX_copy returns to before forming any borrow when to == from.
residuals: BN_MONT_CTX_set_locked's double-checked publication and the caller's lock are unchanged; they are not an aliasing boundary.

boundaries.mechanism: BIGNUM-output borrow ordering in BN_to_montgomery, BN_from_montgomery and BN_mod_mul_montgomery
boundaries.contract: r may alias a or b. Operands are cloned first; the reduced value is computed before r is borrowed, so no shared borrow of the context or operand is live across the write.

boundaries.mechanism: BIGNUM-output borrow ordering in BN_mod_exp_mont, BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime, BN_mod_exp_mont_word and BN_mod_exp2_mont
boundaries.contract: r may alias a, p or m (and, for exp2, any of a1/p1/a2/p2/m). All inputs are cloned (and the CONSTTIME flags read) before r is borrowed. A failed exponentiation leaves r untouched, as before.
residuals: BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime_x2 runs its two exponentiations sequentially. No borrow overlap exists; the second result wins if a caller passes r1 == r2. Cross-triple aliasing is not a supported authority case.

boundaries.contract: RecpCtx and BigNum are distinct object types; no supported alias exists. The divisor is cloned before the context is borrowed.

boundaries.mechanism: reciprocal division and reduction (BN_div_recp, BN_reciprocal, BN_mod_mul_reciprocal)
boundaries.contract: BN_div_recp(dv, rem, m, ...) allows dv == rem (remainder stored first, quotient last) and either output aliasing the dividend m; BN_div reads/clones the dividend before writing. BN_reciprocal allows r == m. BN_mod_mul_reciprocal allows r == x or r == y; both factors are copied before the product is reduced.
residuals: The reciprocal correction loop and its BN_R_BAD_RECIPROCAL site are unchanged.

boundaries.contract: r may alias a, p or m. All three are cloned and their BN_FLG_CONSTTIME bits are read before r is borrowed.
residuals: The even-modulus recp dispatch and the zero-exponent rule (including 0^0 mod 0 == 1) are unchanged.

defects.class: aliasing: `as_mut(r)` and `as_ref(a)`/`as_ref(b)` formed in one tuple, i.e. live mutable and shared borrows of one allocation when a caller aliases an output (a supported case)
defects.description: BN_GF2m_add, BN_GF2m_mod_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_mul_arr, BN_GF2m_mod_sqr_arr and BN_GF2m_mod_exp_arr formed the tuple `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))`. A caller passing the result object as an operand (which the authority allows) made the two borrows alias the same allocation.
defects.fix: Each operand is copied through a scoped shared reference whose last use precedes the output borrow; the output is borrowed only at store time. No operand is read after a partial write. Added the aliased-case control in bn::gf2m::tests.

defects.class: aliasing: two live borrows of one allocation across a call (M18-D1 shape)
defects.description: BN_to_montgomery, BN_from_montgomery, BN_mod_mul_montgomery, BN_mod_exp_mont and BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime formed `(as_mut(r), as_ref(inputs), as_ref_mont(mont))`; BN_MONT_CTX_set formed `(as_mut_mont(mont), as_ref(m))`. The BIGNUM-output cases are reachable with a supported aliased output.
defects.fix: Operands are copied before the output borrow; the reduced value is materialised in a local before `as_mut(r)`, so no context borrow is live across the write. BN_MONT_CTX_set reads the modulus before borrowing the context. BN_MONT_CTX_copy's identity guard and its consequence are documented. Added the aliased-case control in bn::mont::tests.

defects.class: aliasing: two live borrows of one allocation across a call (M18-D1 shape)
defects.description: BN_mod_exp_recp formed `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(p), as_ref(m))`, and then read BN_FLG_CONSTTIME from the same raw inputs while the mutable output borrow was live. A supported r == a/p/m call aliased the borrows.
defects.fix: Inputs are copied and their CONSTTIME flags read before `as_mut(r)`; the output is borrowed at each store. BN_RECP_CTX_set reads its divisor before borrowing the context. Added the aliased-case control in the cfg-gated bn::recp::tests module, including dv == rem and dv == dividend.

defects.lines_post_fix: the # Safety sections of every repaired entry point
defects.class: contract documentation: the old text said `uniquely-owned BIGNUM` although the authority and the implementation accept an aliased output
defects.description: A caller could not tell from the contract that r == a/b/p/m is supported, and the implementation's old borrow shape made the documented-safe call unsound.
defects.fix: Every repaired public entry point now states exactly which arguments may alias and what the aliased result is; the context setters state that their context/modulus are distinct types.

defects.class: same tuple shape with a type-distinct second operand
defects.description: BN_MONT_CTX_set, BN_MONT_CTX_copy and BN_RECP_CTX_set formed a mutable context borrow alongside a shared borrow of a different object type. No supported input can make the two pointers alias, and BN_MONT_CTX_copy already returned early for to == from; the shape is reordered and documented for consistency and to remove the pattern from the three files.
defects.fix: Read-first for the BigNum operand; BN_MONT_CTX_copy's identity guard is documented as the reason its two same-type references are distinct.

public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_add(r, a, b): r == a, r == b or r == a == b is supported; the XOR is computed from the originals and stored last (a + a == 0).
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_mod_arr(r, a, p): r == a is supported; the result is a mod p.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_mod_mul_arr(r, a, b, p): r == a or r == b is supported; a == b takes the square path; the result is a*b mod p.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_mod_sqr_arr(r, a, p): r == a is supported; the result is a^2 mod p.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_mod_exp_arr(r, a, b, p): r == a or r == b is supported; the result is a^b mod p.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_GF2m_mod_inv(r, a, p, ctx): r == a is supported; the read-before-write order holds through the blinded sequence.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_to_montgomery(r, a, mont, ctx): r == a is supported; the result is a*R mod m.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_from_montgomery(r, a, mont, ctx): r == a is supported; the result is a*R^-1 mod m.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_mul_montgomery(r, a, b, mont, ctx: r == a or r == b is supported; the result is a*b*R^-1 mod m.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_exp_mont(r, a, p, m, ctx, in_mont: r == a, r == p or r == m is supported; the result is a^p mod m from the original operands.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime(...): same alias set and result as BN_mod_exp_mont.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_exp_mont_word(r, a, p, m, ...): r == p or r == m is supported.
r may alias any input; all are copied before the store.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_exp_recp(r, a, p, m, ctx): r == a, r == p or r == m is supported; the result is a^p mod m from the original operands.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_div_recp(dv, rem, m, recp, ctx): dv == rem is supported and the shared object ends holding the quotient (remainder stored first); either output may alias the dividend m, which is read first.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_reciprocal(r, m, len, ctx): r == m is supported; the divisor is read before r is written.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_mul_reciprocal(r, x, y, recp, ctx: r == x or r == y is supported; the factors are copied before the reduction.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_MONT_CTX_set(mont, m, ctx) / BN_RECP_: no alias is supported: the context and the BigNum are distinct object types.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_MONT_CTX_copy(to, from): to == from returns to untouched before any borrow; otherwise to and from are distinct.

compatibility.aliased_output_calls: now defined in Rust and equal to the authority's value for every case the authority supports; no API was weakened and no supported aliased case was removed
